transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-13
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~44 mins
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Reyes (Procurement, Bloomfield), Tom Hargreaves (Security Architect, Bloomfield), Priya Nair (Legal Counsel, Bloomfield)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Kickoff to align procurement + security on onboarding path, MSA/DPA points, SLA expectations and pricing approvals.
- Customer requested explicit vendor onboarding appendix, KMS/HSM options, and a benchmark for private deployment.
- Next steps: Redwood to share MSA appendix, run bench, customer to send DPA redlines and gating checklist.

Topics:
- Onboarding path / gating checklist
- MSA & DPA redline expectations
- SLA and uptime/latency targets (dedicated vs hosted)
- Pricing approval flow and billing model (committed vs pay-as-you-go)
- Security controls: KMS, SSO, SOC 2, RBAC, data residency
- Technical benchmark plan for private deployment

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Alicia, Tom, Priya — thanks for squeezing us in. We'll run through procurement requirements, the MSA/DPA high points, and then Samir will go into the technical gating stuff.
[00:00:14] Alicia (Procurement): Yep, thanks. We're short on time so gotta cover the gating checklist, billing path, and any security blockers up front.
[00:00:20] Samir (Redwood SE): quick note, I'll try to keep the deep tech light first, then we can dive on the benchmark plan.
[00:00:28] Priya (Legal): I have a list of DPA items that are non-negotiable for us, like subprocessor lists and data deletion timelines. We'll share.
[00:00:34] Tom (Security): Also want to confirm KMS integration and whether keys are customer-managed in private deployment.
[00:00:40] Maya: Right — high-level, Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For regulated data you folks flagged private. We usually include a vendor onboarding appendix in the MSA for private deployments — that spells out entitlements, access, and incident response.
[00:00:55] Alicia: That onboarding appendix is exactly what procurement needs. We need a clear path: what approvals, SSO setup, who signs off on entitlements, and the billing owner.
[00:01:05] Maya: Understood. We'll add a swimlane diagram in the appendix — who's approver, who provides attestation, timeline to prod.
[00:01:11] Priya: On DPA, two things: data residency guarantees and clarity on subprocessors. We can't have unconstrained subprocessor additions; need notification and 30 days to object. Also encryption at rest with customer-managed keys or HSM.
[00:01:26] Samir: For Private we support customer-managed KMS via the provider's HSM or through an on-prem KMS tunnel; we'll detail the integration steps. Small caveat: if you choose host-managed keys for Hosted, that is different from Private.
[00:01:38] Tom: We'd prefer customer-managed keys. Also we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that possible?
[00:01:44] Samir: Yes, we can forward audit logs; there's an option to ship to your Log endpoint or S3 and we can set retention. We'll document retention windows and fields.
[00:01:52] Alicia: Billing — we need to determine if this goes through committed capacity contract or usage billing. Our finance wants committed monthly for predictability but legal and security want to retain fallback on hosted during spikes.
[00:02:05] Maya: Common pattern: a Dedicated or Private commit for base throughput plus burst to Hosted. We can show committed pricing vs burst rates in the pricing sheet.
[00:02:14] Priya: On SLA — what's Redwood's standard uptime and latency SLOs for Private? We need SLA language for the MSA.
[00:02:21] Samir: For Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptimes, usually 99.9% for capacity nodes; Private SLA can be negotiated — depends on the support tier and infra model (VPC vs on-prem). We'll propose a baseline and a remediation table in the MSA.
[00:02:35] Tom: And data deletion? If we terminate, what does deletion look like for cached KV or logs?
[00:02:40] Maya: We'll add a data termination clause with a timeline — typical is deletion from live systems within X days and certificate of deletion for logs upon request.
[00:02:48] Priya: Please put exact days. We need 30 days for deletion of production data and 90 days for backups, unless we agree otherwise.
[00:02:55] Maya: Noted. We'll draft that.
[00:03:01] Alicia: Ok can we pivot to the procurement gating checklist — what do you need from us to move to legal review?
[00:03:07] Samir: From a tech standpoint: network diagram, proposed instance sizes, expected QPS, and any PII flagging rules. For security: SOC 2 type II report, pen test results, and KMS attestation. For legal: DPA redlines and any claused versions you require.
[00:03:23] Alicia: Timeline wise — procurement wants to lock the vendor by end of month. We need the legal package next week to stay on track.
[00:03:29] Maya: We'll get the MSA appendix and security pack to you by Thursday.
[00:03:34] Priya: Thursday works. I will send initial DPA redlines before then so you can slot them in.
[00:03:39] Tom: Want to flag that we will request an audit rights window. Not full continuous audit but access for yearly audits.
[00:03:46] Maya: Audit rights — yes; we'll include a standard audit clause and, if needed, a controlled-assessment process for Private.
[00:03:52] Speaker 2 (transcription noise): mm-hmm
[00:03:56] Samir: If I can drill in a bit on the benchmark plan — since you mentioned private, we'll need a short POC to validate tail latency and throughput for typical sequences and KV-cache hit rates.
[00:04:08] Tom: Can you simulate our longest sequences? The product team is sensitive to worst-case latencies around 4k tokens.
[00:04:16] Samir: Yes. We'll run two passes: one at expected median sequences and another stress run for long-tail sequences. We'll include KV cache warmup scenarios; Redwood runtime has continuous batching which affects cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:04:30] Priya: Are there any special controls for data used in the benchmark? We can't send prod PII without anonymization.
[00:04:36] Samir: We'll use synthetic datasets that mimic your token distributions. If you want env parity we can run in a VPC with your test data under NDA.
[00:04:45] Alicia: Finance needs to see the billing path — send committed vs usage examples and what Uplift for burst to hosted looks like.
[00:04:52] Maya: We'll include a table with monthly committed baseline, overage rates, and a separate column for hosted burst pricing.
[00:04:59] Alicia: Good. Also we have to route this through our vendor gating tool — they expect a copy of SOC 2 + pricing + MSA appendix + technical contact.
[00:05:06] Maya: We'll make a single bundle PDF for you.
[00:05:10] Tom: One question about RBAC — does Redwood support fine-grained roles, like developer vs ops vs read-only audit?
[00:05:16] Samir: Yes, RBAC exists with role templates; in Private we can add custom roles. There is SSO/SAML support for provisioning via SCIM as well.
[00:05:25] Priya: We'll want SAML + SCIM for user provisioning. Also, single tenancy concerns — we need assurance of tenant isolation.
[00:05:32] Maya: Private gives you tenant-level isolation. We'll include architecture notes showing network segmentation, VPC peering, and isolation boundaries.
[00:05:40] Speaker 1 (ambient): right
[00:05:44] Samir: On encryption at rest — if you insist on customer-managed keys, we'll outline the KMS flow: key rotation, access logs in KMS, and how we (Redwood) sign for ephemeral compute with no long-term access to plaintext keys.
[00:05:56] Tom: That model sounds good. Need to ensure no key escrow by vendor.
[00:06:01] Maya: Agreed; we'll state key ownership clearly.
[00:06:06] Alicia: Switching back to legal approvals — Priya, what redlines are top priority?
[00:06:11] Priya: Subprocessors notification, data deletion timelines, limitation of liability caps — we need these to line up with our enterprise risk profile. Also export controls language — we operate in EMEA and need clarity.
[00:06:24] Maya: We'll flag export controls and include suitable language.
[00:06:29] Samir: A quick note on maintenance windows and scheduled downtime — for Dedicated we can schedule patch windows; for Private, depending on model, we can align to your change window.
[00:06:40] Tom: We need at least two weeks notice for maintenance that could affect latency.
[00:06:44] Maya: We'll draft a maintenance notice policy.
[00:06:49] Alicia: Ok — procurement gating items recap: MSA appendix, SOC2, pricing sheet, AR/PO terms, technical contact and test plan. Any other artifacts?
[00:06:58] Samir: Pen test summary and architecture diagram.
[00:07:01] Alicia: Good.
[00:07:04] Priya: Regarding SLA credits — we want a clearly defined credit table and SLO measurement endpoint.
[00:07:12] Maya: We'll propose SLO measurement via a shared telemetry endpoint with agreed metrics; credits table will be standard.
[00:07:19] [00:07:19] (small crosstalk)
[00:07:25] Samir: Any blockers on export controls? Some of your EMEA nodes may require data residency constraints, we can pin region-specific nodes.
[00:07:34] Tom: Yes, we need EU-only processing for certain data classes.
[00:07:38] Maya: We'll capture data residency options: EU-only for some tenants, US for others — this will be in the appendix and DPA.
[00:07:46] Alicia: Pricing approval flow — how does Redwood prefer to handle PO vs invoice?
[00:07:51] Maya: We accept both. For committed capacity there's a monthly invoice with a contract number; for hosted usage we can bill monthly or on-demand with net-30 terms. We can adapt to your AR.
[00:08:03] Alicia: Finance prefers invoice with net-45, any issue?
[00:08:06] Maya: We can negotiate net-45 for enterprise accounts; we'll put that in the term sheet.
[00:08:12] Priya: A small point — we'd like to see indemnity language for IP claims related to model outputs.
[00:08:18] Maya: Understood, we'll include IP indemnity language in the MSA draft.
[00:08:23] Tom: On the technical bench — do you need agent access or just an API key scoped to a test environment?
[00:08:30] Samir: API key scoped to a test VPC is fine. For on-prem we may need a small agent, but that's only for air-gapped scenarios.
[00:08:38] Alicia: Are there any up-front fees for Private deployment?
[00:08:42] Maya: There's usually an onboarding setup fee that covers deployment and security hardening; we'll include that as optional in the pricing sheet.
[00:08:50] Alicia: Can you ballpark the setup fee?
[00:08:52] Maya: Roughly in the tens of thousands depending on scope; we'll provide a range and a fixed proposal after the benchmarks.
[00:08:59] Speaker 3 (background): okay
[00:09:03] Priya: Export controls again — if model weights or config are considered export-controlled, how does Redwood handle distribution?
[00:09:11] Samir: For Private/on-prem we don't distribute network access to weights; for Dedicated we keep weights in region and can gate based on geo. We'll put export-control language in the MSA as an option.
[00:09:24] Alicia: Ok, let's capture a crisp next-step list to pass to procurement.
[00:09:29] Maya: I'll read the list: 1) MSA vendor onboarding appendix draft (Maya) 2) Pricing sheet with committed/burst examples (Maya) 3) Security pack: SOC2, pen test, KMS integration doc (Samir) 4) Benchmark plan and scheduling (Samir) 5) DPA redlines from Priya (Priya) 6) Procurement gating checklist confirmed (Alicia)
[00:09:54] Priya: I'll send the DPA redlines by Tuesday.
[00:09:57] Alicia: Procurement will review the bundle and aim to put vendor on the next vendor approval board by Oct 27.
[00:10:05] Maya: Great. Any other concerns?
[00:10:08] Tom: One last item — incident response times and escalation contacts; we need 24/7 for sev1s and an escalation tree.
[00:10:15] Maya: We'll include a contact matrix and response SLAs in the appendix.
[00:10:19] Samir: Also for the bench we'll include a list of telemetry fields we'll capture so you can validate SLO metrics.
[00:10:25] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:10:28] [00:10:28] (brief silence)
[00:10:35] Maya: Quick question — competitors you considered? Alicia earlier mentioned Anthropic?
[00:10:41] Alicia: Yes, we looked at Anthropic and considered internal hosting. Anthropic's docs were missing some enterprise deployment options.
[00:10:49] Maya: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood's private option differs.
[00:10:55] Samir: If I can add, for the bench we'll show quantization and batching impacts on cost so you can weigh committed vs hosted economics.
[00:11:05] Tom: That will be helpful for our cost modelling.
[00:11:08] Maya: Ok, logistics — I'll send the MSA appendix and pricing sheet Thursday, Samir will send the bench plan and security pack on the same day. Priya will get DPA redlines to us Tuesday. Alicia you'll route to vendor gating.
[00:11:22] Alicia: Yep. One ask — can you include a short one-page summary for our exec sponsor?
[00:11:28] Maya: We'll prepare a one-pager that highlights risk, cost, timeline, and recommended next steps.
[00:11:33] Priya: Also cc legal on the bundle.
[00:11:36] Maya: Will do.
[00:11:39] [00:11:39] (typing sounds)
[00:11:44] Speaker 2: okay
[00:11:49] Samir: Technical detail note — the KV cache persists only per-session unless configured to persist. We'll document options for cache TTL and eviction so you can control data retention.
[00:12:03] Tom: Good — need TTL control.
[00:12:06] Samir: Another note: for EU-only processing we can pin inference nodes to eu-west-1, locks data in-region and disable cross-region backups unless explicitly enabled.
[00:12:17] Alicia: That's essential.
[00:12:20] Maya: Anything else before we wrap?
[00:12:24] Priya: No, we'll look for the doc bundle.
[00:12:28] Alicia: Procurement will expect the packet by Thursday for board review.
[00:12:33] Maya: Great — last recap in one sentence: Redwood sends MSA appendix + pricing + security pack + bench plan; Bloomfield sends DPA redlines and gating checklist; then schedule bench. Agreed?
[00:12:46] All: Agreed.
[00:12:49] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and Slack.
[00:12:54] [00:12:54] (call ends?)
